title: Visual-explanation spec
description: A structured description of a visual that would teach one question family (SESSION 009 / SPEC-PYQ-002). This is a SPEC, not a final image: it describes what a diagram would show, its metaphor, and the relationships and steps that MUST appear, plus what MUST NOT appear so the visual does not mislead. Rendering these into actual images is a later session. A visual is an analysis over a family's T2 evidence and is never T1_OFFICIAL. Validated by hand-written checks in tests/pyq/test_pyq_intelligence.py (D-0006).

family_id.description: The family this visual teaches. Must resolve to a real family record.

metaphor.description: The everyday picture the diagram evokes (e.g. 'a set being a box; a subset a box inside it').

numbers_relationships.description: Key numbers and the relationships between them the visual must make legible.

must_appear.description: Elements that MUST be in the visual. A visual missing any of these fails its spec.

step_sequence.description: The ordered steps the visual walks a solver through.

recognition_clue.description: What in the visual a solver should associate with this family, so it becomes instantly recognisable.

common_confusion.description: The nearby family a learner might mistake this for, and what the visual must make visually distinct.

memory_anchor.description: A memorable hook (phrase, colour, shape) tied to the concept.

must_not_appear.description: What the visual MUST NOT show or imply, to avoid teaching a wrong relationship. Required — a positive spec alone is insufficient.

color_roles.description: If colours are used, which meaning each colour carries. Optional; null if the spec is monochrome.

source_document_ids.description: Paper IDs whose questions this visual explains.

expert_source_ref.description: Required iff analysis_origin == EXPERT_SOURCED; not Instagram or YouTube.

invariants: family_id must resolve to a real family record
must_appear is non-empty; a visual with nothing required to appear has no spec
analysis_origin == EXPERT_SOURCED  =>  provenance.expert_source_ref is non-null and is not an Instagram or YouTube URL
a visual is never T1_OFFICIAL and never represents a pattern across questions as official policy
must_not_appear covers the misleading over-generalisation and the common wrong relationship, not merely styling
